transcript: Hold the lane. The network stays ours. Nobody crosses while we stand watch. Keep your eyes up and your cell steady. We stabilize the grid together, or we lose everything.

timing.source: espeak-ng libespeak-ng synthesis events (espeakINITIALIZE_PHONEME_EVENTS) via work/espeak_timing.c
timing.positions: milliseconds in the generated audio; 1 ms exact

method: Audio is one continuous espeak-ng synthesis of the full transcript (natural prosody, punctuation pauses included; energy-measured speech region [0.030, 13.180] s). Word, phoneme and clause timings are taken directly from the synthesizer's own event stream: work/espeak_timing.c links libespeak-ng, re-synthesizes the identical text/voice/speed/pitch with phoneme events enabled and dumps WORD/SENTENCE/END/PHONEME events with millisecond audio positions; the helper's generated audio is verified byte-identical to the CLI WAV, so event positions map 1:1 onto this file's timeline (the delivered WAV is the CLI output resampled 22050->44100 Hz; resampling preserves time). The event stream arrives in audio order and every event's span runs to the next event's position (any type), so it tiles the whole utterance: word slots are [WORD event, next WORD event), a word's speech ends where its last phoneme ends, and all inter-word / inter-clause silence is carried by pause phonemes ('_:' clause pause, '_!' word gap, '_' lead-in); this slot model was verified against the audio (the gaps measure ~0 RMS). Word identity comes from WORD events (1-based character position + length); clause slots run from the clause's first WORD event to its END event. The phoneme name sequence is cross-checked against espeak-ng -x. Phonemes map to visemes via phoneme_to_viseme; viseme_to_jaw_open matches tools/rig_ops.py VISEMES. Frame numbers are 1-based at 30 fps; frame f covers [(f-1)/30, f/30) seconds. Event positions are exact (1 ms); no envelope estimation is used.
